overall: The AG found the ARPA committee, formed by Select Board vote and staffed by town department heads, is a subcommittee subject to the OML and violated it by failing to create and maintain minutes. Notice and open-meeting claims were untimely and not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the ARPA committee failed to post notice for its meetings; the Committee argued the complaint was untimely.
allegations.key_passage: we agree that the complaint was untimely with respect to the allegations that the Committee failed to post meeting notices and failed to hold meetings open to the public

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the ARPA committee failed to hold its meetings open to the public.
allegations.key_passage: we agree that the complaint was untimely with respect to the allegations that the Committee failed to post meeting notices and failed to hold meetings open to the public

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the ARPA committee failed to create and maintain minutes of its meetings; the Committee did not dispute it.
allegations.key_passage: we find that it violated the Law by failing to create and maintain minutes for its past meetings

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 90 days of the letter, create minutes for past meetings and certify compliance to the AG's office.
Create past minutes to the best of its ability, using whatever means are available, including attendees' memories and individual notations.
remedy_passage: we order the Committee, within 90 days of the date of this letter, to create minutes for its past meetings and to certify to our office that it has complied with this order.
